OSAGE BEACH, Mo., Oct. 26, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- What does it mean to build a home at the Lake of the Ozarks with intention? That question is answered in a HelloNation article featuring advice from Custom Home Builder Expert Cole Glascock of Glascock Construction in Osage Beach, Missouri. The article outlines how thoughtful planning and flexible home design can help homeowners create lake properties that serve both current needs and long-term goals. The article explains that many Lake of the Ozarks homes begin as weekend getaways or seasonal retreats but often transition into full-time residences. Designing with that future in mind helps ensure the home can adapt over time. According to the article, intentional planning supports a balance between entertainment, relaxation, and privacy, which are all central to the lake lifestyle. A key focus of the article is floor plan design. It outlines how flexible rooms, open living spaces, and seamless indoor-outdoor connections allow for multi-purpose use. Whether a space is used today as a game room or gym, it can later serve as a guest suite or home office if planned correctly. items.title: Athlete of the Week: Johnny Carriger, Crocker Soccer
items.desc: Share on Facebook Share on Twitter As an underclassman, Johnny Carriger was ready for the moment, scoring a hat trick in Crocker’s district championship game. “I think we just wanted it more,” Johnny said. “They came out
items.body: As an underclassman, Johnny Carriger was ready for the moment, scoring a hat trick in Crocker’s district championship game. “I think we just wanted it more,” Johnny said. “They came out like they were going to win. They went up 2-0 in the first half, and I was like someone’s got to step up. So I did.” It was his second hat trick of the tournament, all while battling illness and injury. “He had a 103 fever at district time to send us to the final,” said Crocker Head Soccer Coach Rich Heenan. “Two weeks prior he had broke his hand and powered through without anything on his hand. [Johnny] played the rest of the season in a full cast.” On top of toughness, scoring goals runs in the family. His older brother, Tristen, put up Laquey’s lone goal in the Hornet’s state semifinal game. Johnny was there watching in the stands. “Whenever he scored it I was like dang, why couldn’t that be me,” Johnny said. Now, Tristen is Crocker’s assistant soccer coach. “I just cannot call him coach,” Johnny said. “It’s just too funny.” “He’s watched me play for years,” Tristen Carriger said. “But now it’s me watching him play.” Johnny is nearing 100 career goals as a varsity starter. 34 of them are in the last 16 games. Tristen gets a front-row view of his brother’s success and more. “He likes to help his teammates and help them figure out how to pass the ball better [or] how to do a soccer move,” Tristen said. “[He] even leads them to getting their first goal.” Johnny has no plans of slowing his scoring spree, but as his brother would wan, he’s turned into a leader on top of a striker.

items.title: Battle Of The Bands! Rocktober Rocks The Lake To Help Local Kids
items.desc: Helping kids at Lake of the Ozarks never sounded so good.
items.body: Helping kids at Lake of the Ozarks never sounded so good. Sponsored by Ozark Coast Kiwanis and Wonderland Camp, the three-day Rocktober Battle of the Bands will bring live music to The Encore Lakeside Grill & Sky Bar, Oct. 23-25, 2026, while raising money for both organizations. The idea came together as Kiwanis looked for another way to raise money for children in the Lake area, particularly older kids whose needs can sometimes be harder to fill at Christmas. A similar event had been held locally in the past, so the group decided to bring the concept back as a new fall fundraiser. From country and classic rock to solo, duo, and trio performers, attendees will get to hear a variety of music and vote for their favorites. Each act will perform a 45-minute set, with sound and lighting provided by the Encore. There will also be cash prizes for the best performers and a spot on the Encore's entertainment calendar next year! Admission is FREE, and it's just $1 per vote . Winners will receive a trophy and bragging rights, while the money raised helps support Ozark Coast Kiwanis and Wonderland Camp . Kiwanis supports Lake-area children through scholarships, youth activities, and grants to nonprofits serving kids, including Wonderland Camp. Allen said the organization continues to see unmet needs, especially among older children around Christmas. "Everybody needs a gift at Christmas," Kiwanis member Marilyn Allen said. Money raised through Rocktober will help Kiwanis continue supporting children and families at Christmas and throughout the year, while also benefiting Wonderland Camp and its work serving children and adults with disabilities. items.title: Sunshine Club learns history at October meeting
items.desc: The Fair Grove Sunshine Club met October 14th at the Fair Grove Senior Center. The members attending were Evelyn Kerby, Marilyn Smith, Robbie Gillet, Holly Barlow, Lynda Hutchison, Carolyn Riggi, […]
items.body: The Fair Grove Sunshine Club met October 14th at the Fair Grove Senior Center. The members attending were Evelyn Kerby, Marilyn Smith, Robbie Gillet, Holly Barlow, Lynda Hutchison, Carolyn Riggi, Mary Terry, Peggy Schletty, Rue Withers, Toni Woffard, Ellen Carter, Pam Meyers & Carol Highfill. Everyone had lunch and the Business Meeting followed. Marilyn Smith gave the History of the Sunshine Club. It was started as the W.P.F.A Club in 1923 which stands for the Women’s Progressive Farmer’s Association. When it disbanded in 1986, the Club wanted to continue on, so it was named the Sunshine Club. The Club has met every month for 103 years. The Club has met in everyone’s homes, and went to many interesting places all over the area. We have toured many educational places and always looked forward to the good meals we have shared in homes, Tea Rooms, Restaurants, and the Senior Center. New members are always welcomed.

items.title: MHS Band Takes Fourth at Ozark Mountain Marching Festival
items.desc: The Marshfield High School marching band recently took a little hometown history on the road and returned home with a fourth-place finish at the Ozark Mountain Marching Festival in Reeds […]
items.body: The Marshfield High School marching band recently took a little hometown history on the road and returned home with a fourth-place finish at the Ozark Mountain Marching Festival in Reeds Spring. The band’s show focused on Route 66, a highway that’s been part of Marshfield’s story for generations. With cars, colorful banners, and music, the students brought that history to life on the field. Joe Thomas, who attended the competition and took photos, said it was his first chance to see the show this season. He was impressed with how everything came together. “There was so much thought put into the show,” Thomas said, praising the music, costumes, and choreography. Marshfield made it through the preliminary round before finishing fourth in the finals. For Thomas, it was fun to see local students showcase their talents while celebrating what makes Marshfield special. “It was one of the best shows I’ve seen, and it was great to watch,” he said.

items.title: Buckles, Boots & Bravery! One Of The Lake's Biggest Fundraisers, CADV Brunch Set For Oct. 28
items.desc: For decades, a Lake of the Ozarks tradition has brought the community together to support survivors of domestic violence and their families. Next week, Citizens Against Domestic Violence is celebrating that milestone with its 25th Annual Brunch.
items.body: For decades, a Lake of the Ozarks tradition has brought the community together to support survivors of domestic violence and their families. Next week, Citizens Against Domestic Violence is celebrating that milestone with its 25th Annual Brunch . The fundraiser is set for Wednesday, Oct. 28, at The Lodge of the Four Seasons in Lake Ozark, bringing together supporters, local businesses, and community members to raise awareness and funds for CADV's work. The annual brunch is more than a meal. It helps support CADV's mission of providing hope, safety, and assistance to survivors of domestic violence and their children throughout the Lake area. Last year’s brunch showed just how much impact the event can have. Nearly 800 people attended the Sock Hop brunch, which raised just over $195,000 in gross unrestricted funds — the highest total in the event’s history. Guests sampled dishes from 36 local restaurants, bid on auction items, and heard directly about the experiences of local survivors and the services CADV provides. This year's "Buckles & Boots for Bravery" theme recognizes the courage of survivors while celebrating the community that continues to stand behind CADV's work. The brunch will take place Oct. 28 at The Lodge of the Four Seasons, 315 Four Seasons Drive in Lake Ozark, from 11 a.m. to 1:15 p.m. Those interested in attending through a table sponsorship can visit cadv-voc.org , click the “Brunch” tab, and complete the sponsorship form. Supporters can also donate online and participate in the event’s auction and fundraising opportunities. For questions, call CADV at 573-346-9630 or email info@cadv-voc.org . Those who cannot attend can still help make the brunch a success by purchasing items from CADV’s Amazon Wish List. Shop the wish list here .

items.title: Helping Women Start Over: Lake Of The Ozarks Nonprofit Offers Hope, Housing And Support
items.desc: For women trying to rebuild their lives, a second chance can begin with something as simple as a safe place to sleep, a working phone, transportation or someone willing to give them an opportunity.
items.body: For women trying to rebuild their lives, a second chance can begin with something as simple as a safe place to sleep, a working phone, transportation or someone willing to give them an opportunity. Women Overcoming Obstacles (WOO), a nonprofit organization, is helping women facing difficult circumstances while working toward establishing a transitional housing facility. The organization assists women leaving incarceration, escaping abusive relationships or beginning independent lives. Its mission is to provide a safe, supportive environment that encourages resilience, personal growth and self-sufficiency. For WOO founder Peggy Albers, that mission is deeply personal. After serving more than 15 years in prison, Albers rebuilt her life and established a successful real estate career at the Lake of the Ozarks. Along the way, she experienced firsthand the barriers women face when starting over. Recognizing those challenges, Albers began helping other women with practical needs, including rent, transportation and telephones. Her personal experiences helped inspire WOO and its commitment to giving women a genuine opportunity for a fresh start. Today, WOO is a Missouri 501(c)(3) nonprofit governed by a board of directors that includes Peggy and Mary Albers, Paula Woods, Terri Cooper, Michelle Cooney and Renden Henson. Although its proposed transitional housing facility is still in development, WOO is already making a difference. The organization assisted 25 women in 2025 and had already helped 26 women in 2026 by July. Each number represents a woman with her own challenges, hopes and dreams. Amy Cole is one of those women. items.title: Two New Troopers Join Missouri Highway Patrol In Lake Of The Ozarks Area
items.desc: Two new troopers have been assigned to Camden & Miller counties, in Missouri State Highway Patrol's Troop F. The troopers are members of the Missouri State Highway Patrol’s 126th Recruit Class that graduated on Friday, October 16, 2026.
items.body: Two new troopers have been assigned to Camden & Miller counties, in Missouri State Highway Patrol's Troop F. The troopers are members of the Missouri State Highway Patrol’s 126th Recruit Class that graduated on Friday, October 16, 2026. Trooper Ashton G. Wise, of Camdenton, MO, has been assigned to Zone 11, which serves the citizens of Camden and Miller counties. In 2022, Tpr. Wise graduated from Camdenton High School in Camdenton, MO. Prior to joining the Patrol, Tpr. Wise was employed by the Green County Sheriff’s Office as a detention officer in Springfield, MO. Trooper Erin K. Bock, of Argyle, MO, has been assigned to Zone 11, which serves the citizens of Camden and Miller counties. In 2022, Trooper Bock graduated from Fatima High School in Westphalia, MO. In 2026, Tpr. Bock earned an Associate of Arts degree in social human behavior from Moberly Area Community College in Columbia, MO.
